title: Proper acyclicity of injectives extended from an arbitrary Cartesian open
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $p:V\to T$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism], let $i:W\hookrightarrow T$ be an arbitrary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and put $U=V\times_TW$, with projections $k:U\hookrightarrow V$ and $r:U\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use sheaves of modules over the constant sheaves of rings $A_H$ on the small pro-etale sites of $H=U,V,W,T$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $p_*,r_*$ and $i^*,k^*$ for direct image and exact inverse image with constant-ring identifications [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and $i_!,k_!$ for extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero].
Assume that there is an integer $d\geq0$ such that $R^qp_*F=0$ for every module sheaf $F$ on $V$ and every $q>d$. For every injective object $J$ of the module category on $U$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], its extension $k_!J$ is $p_*$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic]:
$$R^qp_*(k_!J)=0\qquad(q>0).$$
Here $R^qp_*F=\mathcal H^q(Rp_*(F[0]))$ uses the ordinary uncompleted derived direct image and cohomology sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. No quasi-compactness of $i$ and no etale-origin condition on $J$ is assumed.

split_report.summary: Q102 repairs the dedicated long-step return: replaces former Step 2 by four short steps, extracts canonical weakly-etale pro-etale inverse-image/restriction and coefficient normalization as one new unsplit lemma, and retains principal-open exhaustion as an explicit elementary calculation using existing leaves. All other steps retain their argument with cross-references renumbered. Statement, Lean record, chapter/unit and accepted tool uses are unchanged. Maintainer reader (cc review): the new comparison node duplicated the existing unsplit node lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction (clauses (1)-(3): weakly-etale site-object inverse image is restriction, with the constant-ring structure map and module pullback); the new node is dropped and Step 3 cites the existing node, declared as a tool use.

New Steps 2–5 refine former Step 2; the new comparison lemma serves inverse-image/restriction identification after weakly-etale testing. New Steps 1,6–9 are the old Steps 1,3–6, with cross-references renumbered.

tool_uses.why: Generic enough-injectives and small-colimit existence for the module categories used in the resolution and exhaustion arguments. It is used as a tool without replacing a step of the unit.
Exact module evaluation identifies cohomology sheaf sections with cohomology of the evaluated injective resolution. It is used as a tool without replacing a step of the unit.
Generic slice-site restriction preserves injectives and identifies derived sections after weakly etale restriction. It is used as a tool without replacing a step of the unit.
Generic pro-etale open-extension base change identifies the actual sheaf being tested after weakly etale restriction. It is used as a tool without replacing a step of the unit.
Generic open extension/restriction adjunction proves the exhaustion colimit and composition identities. It is used as a tool without replacing a step of the unit.

Generic bounded-below cohomology continuity, on degree-zero finite-ring module sheaves; no node of the sf-existence unit supplies this filtered-colimit calculation. It is used as a tool without replacing a step of the unit.
Generic detection of zero pro-etale sheaves using affine weakly contractible test objects. It is used as a tool without replacing a step of the unit.
Open immersions give weakly etale localizations and identify restricted constant coefficient rings; this is a generic site tool, not a replacement for the exceptional-adjoint route.

Generic site-theoretic comparison (Stacks sites 03CE applied to pro-etale 09A5): inverse image along a site object g:Y->X is sectionwise restriction, with the constant-ring structure map and module pullback identified. Step 3 takes only its statement to identify (k_!J)|_P and J|_{U_Q} with the actual inverse images; no node of sk-prop-sf-existence states it.
